item.title: 加拿大波特航空航班因儿童拒绝坐下并系好安全带而被取消
item.description:
多伦多（美联社）——上周，波特航空公司在加拿大的一架航班被取消，原因是一名幼儿拒绝坐下并系好安全带，迫使飞机返回航站楼，并延误了机场关闭的跑道。
这家总部位于多伦多的航空公司周日表示，父母和机组人员多次尝试将孩子固定在座位上，但没有成功，然后将飞机返回不列颠哥伦比亚省维多利亚国际机场的航站楼以带走父母和孩子。
波特表示，周四凌晨 12 点 30 分机场跑道关闭后，将父母和孩子及其行李移走，导致飞往多伦多的航班延误，迫使其余乘客下机。
波特向其他乘客道歉，他们在第二天重新预订了航班。

item.title: 官员称，乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯一座城市，造成 13 人死亡，据报道一座炼油厂遭到袭击
item.description:
鞑靼斯坦地区当局称，乌克兰无人机周一对俄罗斯城市下卡姆斯克发动袭击，造成 13 人死亡，其中包括一名儿童，另有 75 人受伤。乌克兰军方表示，袭击了那里的一座炼油厂。
俄罗斯官员没有透露无人机的目标是什么，但该市是一个重要的炼油中心，拥有两家炼油厂和一家石化厂。近几个月来，乌克兰几乎每天都用远程无人机瞄准俄罗斯石油设施。炮火袭击导致俄罗斯燃料短缺，侵蚀了俄罗斯炼油能力，并使俄罗斯公众感到不安。
乌克兰总统泽连斯基表示，这是一场迫使俄罗斯总统普京坐到谈判桌前并阻止其长达四年多的入侵的运动。
据鞑靼斯坦共和国总统鲁斯塔姆·明尼哈诺夫的新闻部门称，下卡姆斯克周一上午遭受了针对工业和民用设施的“大规模”无人机袭击。目前还没有进一步的细节。
乌克兰总参谋部表示，其部队袭击了下卡姆斯克的塔内科炼油厂，引发火灾。
无法独立核实任何一方的说法。
下卡姆斯克位于乌克兰边境以东约 1,200 公里（750 英里）处，人口约 24 万。
乌克兰国内开发的远程无人机在俄罗斯境内飞行的距离越来越远，其中一些现在已经到达距离边境约2,000公里（1,200英里）的西伯利亚。
“我们确实做出了完全合理的反应，俄罗斯的每一次袭击都会得到我们的回应。俄罗斯的战争将越来越多地在他们自己的家乡——俄罗斯感受到，”泽连斯基周日晚间在社交媒体上表示。
“这种情况仍在持续的唯一原因是俄罗斯不愿意结束这场战争。”
据联合国称，俄罗斯还经常使用导弹、威力强大的滑翔炸弹和无人机从空中袭击乌克兰，袭击平民地区，造成数千名平民伤亡。
世界卫生组织欧洲办事处周一表示，其位于乌克兰中部第聂伯罗地区的一个仓库在不到24小时内遭遇两次袭击。
声明称，袭击摧毁了价值约 50 万美元的紧急物资，这些物资本来是为前线医疗设施准备的。没有人员伤亡报告。
关注美联社对乌克兰战争的报道：https://apnews.com/hub/Russia-ukraine

item.title: 纽约港一艘船翻覆，妇女和5个月大婴儿死亡
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——美国海岸警卫队周日表示，一艘在纽约港倾覆并导致一名母亲和她年幼的女儿丧生的船只的操作者正面临刑事指控，当局正在调查该船是否非法包租。
这艘 22 英尺长的 Bayliner 快艇于晚上 10 点 25 分左右倾覆。美国海岸警卫队称，周六在自由女神像所在地自由岛附近。
在警方赶到之前，已有 12 人从水中被救出，警方潜水员随后在水中找到了这名 27 岁的妇女和 5 个月大的女孩。两人都被送往医院，并被宣布死亡。据海岸警卫队称，其他人情况稳定。
纽约海岸警卫队部门指挥官多琳·麦卡锡上尉表示：“我们对昨晚的悲惨生命损失深感悲痛，在这个极其困难的时刻，我们与受害者的家人和亲人同在。”“我们非常感谢我们的合作伙伴机构和好撒玛利亚人船只所采取的英勇而迅速的行动，他们协助营救了水中的幸存者。”
警方称，46 岁的纽约人曼努埃尔·埃尔南德斯 (Manuel Hernandez) 被指控犯有 13 项鲁莽危害罪名。周日没有找到他的电话号码，该案尚未进入网上法庭记录。
警方周日表示，在通知家人之前，受害者的身份尚未公布。
Adam Schwartz 表示，事故发生时，他的观光公司的 Sea the City II 号热水浴缸游船正在巡航，船上有 12 名幸存者。
施瓦茨周日告诉美联社：“我们的船长和两名船员立即提供协助，向海岸警卫队求助，然后……然后与海岸警卫队和纽约警察局港口单位协调，将他们带到布鲁克林登陆。”
麦卡锡表示，海岸警卫队调查人员正在与警方合作进行调查，并致力于追究违法者的责任。根据海岸警卫队的说法，非法包租是指任何缺乏海岸警卫队资质、安全设备和检查证书的客运船只运营。

item.title: 野火席卷美国西部和加拿大，居民被疏散
item.description:
周日，美国西部和加拿大燃烧的野火使一些居民警惕可能的疏散命令，而其他已经被迫逃离家园的人则等待着看看他们回来后会剩下什么。
在加拿大西部，周末，由于快速蔓延的野火摧毁了房屋，超过 20,000 人被迫逃离不列颠哥伦比亚省奥肯那根湖沿岸的社区，数十人不得不通过飞机救援。在美国，华盛顿的工作人员已经在斯波坎地区扑灭了三场野火，这三场野火在斯波坎地区燃烧了一个多星期，他们继续在遏制线附近进行清理工作。
上周末，劳里·艾伦 (Laurie Allen) 离开位于斯波坎北部社区九英里瀑布 (Nine Mile Falls) 的家，带着丈夫、狗和两只小猫逃离了不远处发生的野火。周日，通往她所在社区的道路仍然关闭，但她说她从一位朋友那里得知，虽然她的房子和附近的其他房子都被灰烬覆盖，但都完好无损。
“我在这里已经 65 年了。这从来没有发生过，”艾伦说。“我们没有考虑任何事情，只是抓住我们的动物然后离开。但现在它影响了我们周围的很多朋友和家人。所以这是相当毁灭性的。”
在加拿大，安妮特·博莱特 (Anette Boulet) 是逃离萨默兰 (Summerland) 的居民之一。萨默兰 (Summerland) 位于不列颠哥伦比亚省奥肯那根湖 (Okanagan Lake) 沿岸，居住着约 12,000 人。周六凌晨 4 点 30 分左右，当她和家人离开时，他们的家被烟雾笼罩。
2026 年 8 月 8 日星期六晚，秃岭野火的热点在不列颠哥伦比亚省萨默兰房屋上方的山腰上燃烧。（Darryl Dyck/加拿大媒体，美联社）
“你几乎看不见。当时天很黑，山脊，火山脊正向你袭来，”疏散到彭蒂克顿中心的鲍莱特说。
“没有言语可以表达它，”她说。“恐惧。”
周日晚些时候，加拿大皇家骑警表示，一名 80 岁的妇女在试图逃离奥肯那根湖地区被迫疏散的野火时死亡。
除了萨默兰 (Summerland) 的疏散工作外，周五晚上首次报道的巴尔德山脉 (Bald Range) 火灾也导致皮奇兰 (Peachland) 及其周边地区约 ​​8,000 人疏散。不列颠哥伦比亚省周六宣布进入紧急状态。
加拿大应急管理和社区复原力部长埃莉诺·奥尔谢夫斯基周日在社交媒体上表示，她已批准不列颠哥伦比亚省的联邦援助请求，为被迫逃离的人提供庇护所和住宿。
2026 年 8 月 8 日星期六，在不列颠哥伦比亚省彭蒂克顿，格雷格·克劳特 (Greg Krauter) 因巴尔德山脉 (Bald Range) 野火而被迫在半夜带着七只山羊撤离萨默兰 (Summerland) 的房产，他在卡车后座检查其中的一些山羊，而其他山羊则在不列颠哥伦比亚省彭蒂克顿的一个疏散中心外走动。（Darryl Dyck/加拿大媒体，美联社）
据野火管理团队发布的新闻稿称，周日，扑灭斯波坎地区三场野火的工作人员继续在遏制线附近进行“扫荡行动”，没有任何火势蔓延。上周发生的大火已损坏或摧毁了约 920 座建筑物。
本周早些时候，一名男子被捕并被指控故意纵火，这是斯波坎地区三起火灾中规模最大的一场。
周六，位于斯波坎以南约 35 英里（55 公里）的乡村小镇马尔登的居民被敦促立即撤离。然而，到了周日，他们的疏散级别已降级，准备在必要时迅速撤离。
约翰·戈伊克（John Goyke）的公司根据合同经营马尔登的水，他说：“风势相当平静。火势没有蔓延，但我们正在使用社交媒体和 Facebook 与每个人保持联系。”
附近罗萨莉亚市的市长戈伊克表示，马尔登的居民被告知要节约用水，以便在需要时为消防车节省用水，马尔登消防部门一直在从罗萨莉亚运水。
2020 年，马尔登的大部分地区被野火摧毁，失去了消防站、邮局、市政厅和图书馆。
在犹他州，周五早上，两名直升机飞行员在鱼湖国家森林扑灭野火时坠毁。周六，工作人员终于能够到达现场确认死亡情况。
官员们周日表示，由于地形陡峭、崎岖，火灾导致他们无法迅速到达该地区。
塞维尔县警长内森·柯蒂斯说：“当我们第一次到达那里时，我们可以看到两股不同的烟雾，一股来自坠机现场，一股来自向我们扑来的大火。”
美国国家运输安全委员会正在调查事故原因。
美联社记者霍莉·拉默对此报道做出了贡献。

item.title: 国会民主党人对驱逐美军成员及其家人的行为展开调查
item.description:
国会民主党人表示，在美联社发现超过 50 名现役军人的配偶和父母被移民当局拘留后，他们正在调查特朗普政府驱逐军人及其家人的行为。
民主党在周日晚间致国土安全部、国防部和退伍军人事务部的一封信中表示，他们将调查五角大楼和国土安全部是否正在协调驱逐军人及其家人。
这封由 60 多名议员签署并提供给美联社的信称，“这些行为危及军事准备，削弱军人的士气，违背了美国对那些为国家冒生命危险的人们的承诺。”
五角大楼拒绝置评，表示将“直接回复这封信的作者”。
国土安全部告诉美联社，它重视军人的贡献，“美国兵役本身并不能自动授予合法移民身份，也不能免除外国人违反美国移民法的后果。”
退伍军人管理局没有立即回应置评请求。
民主党在信中向各机构提出了广泛的问题清单。他们表示，国土安全部和军方明显合作驱逐军人家属，“引起了道德和法律方面的担忧”。
马萨诸塞州参议员说：“唐纳德·特朗普撕毁了数十个承诺提供移民保护的军人家庭，破坏了我们国家对军人的承诺。”伊丽莎白·沃伦说道。“这简直太残酷了，它正在损害我们的军事准备和士气。”
沃伦的办公室正在与康涅狄格州参议员一起领导这项调查。理查德·布卢门撒尔 (Richard Blumenthal)，伊利诺伊州参议员。塔米·达克沃斯和几位众议院民主党人。
美联社的调查发现，唐纳德·特朗普总统的政府取消了对军人家属的保护，并背离了两党长期以来达成的大规模驱逐议程的共识。在配偶被拘留后，服役人员被迫休假，包括推迟部署，以照顾孩子。
议员们向政府施压，询问征兵人员为何仍在促进移民保护。
议员们援引美联社的报道，敦促特朗普政府恢复此前保护军人家属免受移民执法影响的政策，同时允许他们调整自己的法律地位。
参议院退伍军人事务委员会资深民主党人布卢门撒尔表示：“这份报告令人震惊，显示了特朗普移民议程核心令人难以置信的残酷行为。”“我们将要求答案和问责。”
武装部队和退伍军人事务委员会的共和党主席、密西西比州参议员。罗杰·威克和堪萨斯州参议员杰里·莫兰没有回应置评请求。
上周，特朗普成立了军事配偶委员会，由国防部长皮特·赫格斯的妻子詹妮弗·劳切特担任主席，负责制定改善军人配偶生活的政策和建议。
特朗普在 8 月 6 日发表在《联邦公报》上的一封信中表示，“军人配偶与我们军队的良好秩序、战备和保留有着内在的联系。他们对我们武装部队的支持和贡献对于任务的成功至关重要。”
白宫没有回应置评请求。
美联社获得的国防部在去年 12 月致民主党议员的一封信中表示，国防部最近没有对军队中的非公民家庭成员实施任何政策变化，也没有对驱逐出境如何影响部队战备和士气进行分析。
为面临驱逐的军人家属和退伍军人提供支持的组织“遣返我们的爱国者”主席达尼察·詹姆斯表示，军队正在遭到背叛。
詹姆斯说：“我们的军人是那些在虚线上签名去保卫我们的国家，但可能不会回来的人。”“他们相信我们的政府会照顾他们的家人，但他们并没有这样做。”
布鲁克是美联社/美国报道州议会新闻计划的成员。美国报道是一项非营利性国家服务计划，让记者在当地新闻编辑室报道未被揭露的问题。

item.title: 特朗普宣布幕僚秘书威尔·沙夫将担任他的新任白宫法律顾问
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——唐纳德·特朗普总统周日宣布，他的新任白宫法律顾问将是幕僚秘书威尔·沙夫（Will Scharf），他作为特朗普任命的国家资本规划委员会主席，帮助确保了这项价值 4 亿美元的宴会厅项目的批准。
特朗普表示，从 9 月 1 日开始，沙夫将接替大卫·沃灵顿，后者将离开政府加入私营部门。特朗普指出，沙夫此前曾担任联邦检察官，并在包括最高法院在内的许多案件中代表他。
“意志是坚韧、坚强和聪明的！他也热爱我们的国家，并尊重法律，”特朗普在《真相社会》上写道。“威尔·沙夫作为白宫法律顾问会做得很好！”
白宫法律顾问办公室的改组正值关键时刻——距离中期选举仅几个月，特朗普领导的共和党将奋力保住国会的控制权。民主党人誓言，如果 11 月调查成功，将对特朗普及其政府展开调查。
白宫法律顾问的工作是就与总统职位相关的法律和政策问题提供建议。该办公室是司法部在白宫的主要联系人，负责处理总统赦免、司法任命和审查立法。该办公室还帮助调查和管理国会对政府的调查以及总统以官方身份被起诉时针对总统的诉讼。
在特朗普的第一个任期内，沙夫努力让法官和大法官得到确认。其中包括美国最高法院法官布雷特·卡瓦诺（Brett Kavanaugh）（他本人曾担任乔治·W·布什总统的白宫幕僚秘书）和艾米·科尼·巴雷特（Amy Coney Barrett）。
在特朗普卸任期间，沙夫于2023年10月加入他的法律团队，并在特别检察官杰克·史密斯提起的选举干扰案中担任他的律师之一。此案提交最高法院，最高法院裁定总统享有全面的豁免权，免受因官方行为而受到刑事起诉。
沙夫是特朗普第二届政府中获得职位的几位律师之一。托德·布兰奇（Todd Blanche）在纽约共和党封口费审判中代表特朗普，上周被确认担任司法部长。
作为白宫幕僚秘书，沙夫负责管理总统办公桌上的文件。当总统签署行政命令时，他站在特朗普身边，并经常对特朗普签署的内容进行连续旁白。
特朗普于 2025 年 7 月任命沙夫为国家首都规划委员会主席，该委员会是负责该地区政府建筑建设和重大翻修的行政部门机构。
特朗普的舞厅于 4 月份获得了 NCPC 的最终批准，尽管联邦上诉法院周五裁定，该项目的建设必须停止，因为国会尚未批准该项目。特朗普发誓要向美国最高法院提起上诉。
该项目已经进展顺利，并开始在白宫东侧拔地而起。

item.title: 明尼苏达州参议院初选惨烈，特朗普的移民镇压迫在眉睫
item.description:
MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — In the streets surrounding a drab federal office complex next to the Minneapolis airport, the beleaguered resistance toPresident Donald Trumpfound its footing.
As U.S. immigration agents staged at the Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building for a monthslongdeportation campaign, protesters with whistles and cellphone cameras assembled to oppose them.Two were shot and killedin the city’s streets before Trump pulled back under pressure.
Months later, those confrontations remain the backdrop to Minnesota’sDemocratic primary for U.S. Senateon Tuesday, which features establishment-backed U.S. Rep. Angie Craig and the more progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan. The immigration debate is an added schism in a race that otherwise echoes many of the other left versus center divides that have played out across the United States this year.
Protesters stand on the side of the road with ICE protest signs, Jan. 19, 2026, in St. Paul, Minn. (AP Photo/Angelina Katsanis, File)
Craig voted for tighter enforcement soon after Trump returned to office last year, only to later express regret for her decision after the Republican president sent a surge of agents into Minneapolis. She backed a resolution that condemned antisemitism after a2025 firebombingin Boulder, Colorado, and expressed thanks for law enforcement, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers.
Those votes may turn out to be some of the most fraught of Craig’s eight-year career in Congress, decisions that Flanagan has highlighted while trying to portray her rival as unwilling to fight an unpopular administration in Washington.
“I think that’s when she lost my vote permanently and that’s why I will not vote for her no matter what,” said Bryce Bohne, 40, of Minneapolis. The teacher and owner of an educational tourism company is supporting Flanagan.
Around the Whipple federal building, the fences and barriers are down. The ambient soundtrack is no longer the whistles and chants of protesters, just the rumble of departing jets and passing buses.
But the signs of what happened remain. A few volunteers in bright orange vests keep vigil across the street for 12-plus hours a day, ready to help people getting released from immigration detention or leaving hearings at the immigration court inside.
A few miles away, visitors still bring fresh flowers and handwritten notes to memorials marking the spotswhere Renee GoodandAlex Prettiwere killed.
A demonstrator holds a sign reading “Justice for Renee & Alex” during a protest outside a SpringHill Suites and Residence Inn by Marriott hotels, Jan. 26, 2026, in Maple Grove, Minn. (AP Photo/Adam Gray, File)
Craig flipped a Republican-held seat in 2018, and every two years she overcame millions of dollars of attack ads to win tough reelection campaigns.
Until Craig’s Senate run, the heat came from the right. Newly under fire from the other side, the decisions she made as a swing-seat congresswoman have become a liability as a statewide Senate candidate. At one recent event, she adopted the language of the insurgent left, though it did not always seem to come naturally.
“The working class keeps getting screwed,” she told volunteers preparing to knock on doors for her Saturday in Brooklyn Park, a Minneapolis suburb. “Folks, I don’t know about you, but it is time that we had a working folks reno— reso— renovation—"
U.S. Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., a candidate for U.S Senate, speaks to constituents during a door-knocking event Saturday, July 25, 2026, in Minneapolis. (AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt)
In Craig’s view, she is well suited to the antiestablishment fervor gaining a foothold in the Democratic Party. Raised by a single mother in an Arkansas trailer park, she has known economic hardship. The lesbian mother of four grown children, she is not the archetype of a traditional member of Congress.
She was one of the House Democrats to call for President Joe Biden to drop out of the 2024 race after his disastrous debate performance against Trump. As a relatively junior member of Congress, she pushed successfully to become the top Democrat on the Agriculture Committee, jumping ahead of long-tenured colleagues.
“I consider myself a progressive” she told reporters after her event Saturday. “Every race that I run, Republicans run ads against me saying I vote with Democrats 96, 97% of the time.”
“Of course, in the primary,” she added, “people want to point out the few votes I’ve taken against Democrats.”
Chief among them was theLaken Riley Act, the first bill passed by Congress after Trump started his second term. It requires federal authorities to detain migrants accused of theft and violent crimes.
Craig and nearly 60 other Democrats in the House and Senate voted for the bill early in 2025.
But at the end of the year, as immigration officers descended on Minneapolis, that vote became a liability. Weeks after Good and Pretti were killed, Craig published a mea culpa in a Minnesota Star Tribune column.
Craig explained that although she had qualms with parts of the law, it had the support of Democrats she respected, and many of her constituents were unhappy with the situation on the border under Biden.
But the “outright occupation by aggressive, unaccountable federal forces” made clear to her “that supporting any bill that gives ICE new authority in this administration was the wrong decision. And I regret my vote.”
Trump’s immigration operation, she says, was not enabled by her vote on the Laken Riley Act.
“Before that, people had a little bit more sensibility about the fact she was in a tough district and had to take tough votes,” said Corey Day, former executive director of the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party.
Craig has since presented herself as a strong defender of Minnesotans against Trump. She says her record of winning tough races positions her to ensure the seat stays in Democratic hands.
“Angie has experience working across demographics that we need to win over statewide, including in rural Minnesota,” said Kevin Anderson, a Hennepin County commissioner who is supporting Craig and went to one of her weekend events. “I love Peggy, I really do, she’s a great politician. But I don’t think she’s ever had to work across Minnesota.”
Democratic Gov. Tim Walz has declined to endorse either candidate for the seat held by Democrat Tina Smith, who is not running again. Late last month his wife, Gwen Walz, endorsed Craig over Flanagan, his governing partner for two terms.
The Republican field includesMichele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter.
Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate, listens to a voter during a campaign event at the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe Twin Cities Office in Minneapolis, Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt)
To Flanagan and her supporters, Craig’s vote for the immigration bill was not a pragmatic overture to swing voters but a betrayal.
“My primary opponent voted for Donald Trump’s immigration bill and was the only Minnesota Democrat to do so,” Flanagan told volunteers in St. Paul on Saturday. “She since then has said that she regrets that vote, and I’m glad. But it shouldn’t have taken 14 months.”
“We can stand with the immigrant community and not just when it’s politically expedient for us,” Flanagan added.
Like Abdul El-Sayed, who won last week’s Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, Flanagan supports Medicare for All and wants to curtail U.S. military support for Israel. She is running as much against the donors who have spent millions of dollars backing Craig as she is against Craig herself.
“The fact that the money is coming from us and only us makes such a huge difference, because she’s beholden to us, not some billionaire with some business or crypto interest,” said 43-year-old Flanagan supporter Justin Ropella, a customer service manager from Woodbury.
Through July 22, Craig’s campaign had spent $9 million and Flanagan’s $5.5 million. The disparity was even higher among outside groups, with Craig backers spending considerably more, though both have benefited from an influx of outside spending.
To help make up the difference, Flanagan has called on the support of progressive champions such as Sen. Bernie Sanders the Vermont independent who campaigned with her last month.
“If the people of Minnesota can stand up -- and I’m confident that they can -- and tell these billionaires and their lies and their 30-second ads and their super PACs to go to hell, democracy is going to reign,” Sanders said.

item.title: 埃尔-赛义德与奥巴马进行了交谈，密歇根州民主党人希望在激烈的参议院初选后团结起来
item.description:
新泽西州布里奇沃特（美联社）——密歇根州美国参议院民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德周日表示，他已与巴拉克·奥巴马进行了交谈，并希望这位前总统与他一起竞选，因为该党在经历了一场痛苦的初选后试图团结起来，这场初选暴露了进步派和温和派之间的深刻裂痕。
埃尔-赛义德表示，他周五与奥巴马的谈话“非常温暖且鼓舞人心”。该候选人没有提供细节。
“我很感激他的建议。这非常热情，非常吸引人，我知道他知道密歇根州将发挥的关键作用，”埃尔-赛义德告诉 NBC 的“会见媒体”节目。
当被问及他是否希望看到奥巴马在 11 月中期选举前来到密歇根州为民主党争取支持时，埃尔-赛义德表示，他“真的”希望如此，而且奥巴马在 2008 年和 2012 年总统竞选中赢得密歇根州后，“对赢得密歇根州了解很多”。
奥巴马发言人证实了这一电话。
讨论发生的同一天，一群密歇根州提名者和其他著名的全国民主党人试图在底特律的一次集会上表现出统一战线。人群为前公共卫生官员埃尔赛义德欢呼最响亮，他上周在一场备受争议且备受关注的初选中以微弱优势击败了建制派支持的美国众议员海莉·史蒂文斯。民主党在秋季的胜利对于该党重新获得参议院多数席位的机会至关重要。
民主党参议员加里·彼得斯 (Gary Peters) 并不寻求在这个常年摇摆州连任，共和党人唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 在 2016 年和 2024 年赢得了这个州，而民主党人乔·拜登 (Joe Biden) 在 2020 年赢得了该州的胜利。
埃尔-赛义德的对手是共和党人迈克·罗杰斯(Mike Rogers)，这位前国会议员在 2024 年的参议院竞选中以微弱优势输给了民主党人埃丽莎·斯洛特金 (Elissa Slotkin)，并试图利用民主党内部挥之不去的紧张局势。
罗杰斯发布了一段视频信息，试图吸引那些认为自己的政党可能与埃尔-赛义德走得太左的民主党人。“你和我们在一起有一个家，”罗杰斯在视频中说道。
在周日接受美国有线电视新闻网“国情咨文”采访时，埃尔-赛义德承认，在激烈的初选中“我们表达了我们的分歧”。但他表示，内部分歧“比我们的相似之处要小得多”。
“你会看到人们走到一起，”埃尔-赛义德在谈到温和的民主党人之前说道，“我们可能会以不同的方式看待世界。但我们也认识到走到一起的责任。”

item.title: 勇士队王牌克里斯·塞尔在对阵洋基队的比赛开始前被裁判丹·默泽尔驱逐出场
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——在周日对阵纽约洋基队的比赛中，亚特兰大勇士队的王牌球员克里斯·塞尔在投球前被裁判丹·默泽尔驱逐出场，一天前，他因投球得分而被吹罚投球。
当裁判员走上球场，走过勇士队三垒一侧的休息区时，塞尔开始吠叫。默泽尔把他扔了下去，塞尔对机组长丹·贝利诺说了些什么，两人在休息室栏杆附近交谈。
“我在球棒架旁，因为比赛即将开始，我正在拿头盔，”中外野手迈克尔·哈里斯二世在他的第 10 局单打帮助亚特兰大队以 2-1 获胜后说道。“我没有看到他在和他说话，但我实际上看到了他把他扔出去的动作。我有点困惑，但后来我看到了塞尔，想起了昨天发生的事情，我把两个和两个放在一起。”
在周六5-4输掉比赛的第五局中，塞尔被梅泽尔吹罚职业生涯第三次击球。新秀斯宾塞·琼斯在打点三垒安打后击球得分，塞尔开始对默泽尔猛烈地大喊大叫，随后主教练沃尔特·韦斯继续争吵并被驱逐。
“我认为他昨天对裁判说了一些话，但你知道吗，一切都已经过去了，”韦斯说。“每个人都有自己的发言权，我们继续前进。”
贝利诺在周六的比赛结束后告诉台球记者，塞尔被要求回避，因为他没有宣布自己要在比赛结束时投球。贝利诺表示，塞尔在三振何塞·卡巴列罗时宣称自己即将投球，但在击球给奥斯汀·威尔斯之前并没有这样做。
这是塞尔职业生涯第四次被驱逐。这是他自 2019 年 8 月 3 日以来的第一次，当时他为波士顿队投球，在洋基体育场以 9-2 输掉比赛的第四局中，因争球和好球而被迈克·埃斯塔布鲁克 (Mike Estabrook) 扔下。
塞尔周六在六局比赛中失三分、五支安打，这是他自 6 月 28 日以来的第一次失利。在他为勇士队效力的第三个赛季中，这位经验丰富的左手投手在 21 场先发中取得了 12 胜 7 负的战绩，自责失分率为 2.20。

item.title: 效力凯尔特人队期间赢得 5 次总冠军的 NBA 教练唐·尼尔森去世，享年 86 岁
item.description:
Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history who won five championships as a player with theBoston Celtics, died Sunday. He was 86.
Nelson’s family confirmed thedeathin a statement that did not say where he died or provide a cause.
“On Sunday morning our beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family,” the statement said. “Throughout his last week, friends and family encircled him with love, sharing the blessing of his friendship and revisiting treasured memories.”
Nelson is one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with three different franchises —Milwaukee,DallasandGolden State— also serving as general manager for all three franchises. He was a three-time coach of the year and made the playoffs 18 times in 31 seasons. He went to the conference finals three times with the Bucks and once with the Mavericks, never winning a title.
Nelson introduced what is now known as the point forward, and his up-tempo style of offense created a buzz. He said the idea of shifting from the dominant big men of the 1970s to an offense focused on speed and the fast break came from his playing days under Celtics Hall of Fame coach Red Auerbach.
“The league really hadn’t seen an offense like the one we were running, and the results were undeniable,” Nelson wrote in 2016 in The Players’ Tribune.
Nelson said that “without Red Auerbach teaching me the mechanics of running the fast break, none of it would have been possible. He deserves all the credit for Nellie Ball, and for how fast the game of basketball is played today.”
Nelson played 11 of his 14 seasons in Boston and was on five Celtics championship teams under four different coaches. He became an assistant coach in Milwaukee after retiring as a player, then took over after coach Larry Costello resigned 18 games into the 1976-77 season. Nelson coached the Bucks for 11 seasons starting in 1976 and won seven straight division titles.
In Nelson’s second season, Milwaukee overcame a 29-point fourth quarter deficit to beat Atlanta 117-115 in regulation.
“I coached the team as though I was still playing for the Celtics, while implementing a few of my own strategies,” Nelson wrote. “I knew I wanted to play unconventional basketball and use speed to my advantage.”
His fast-paced offenses were probably best on display with Golden State in the “Run TMC” era featuring future Hall of Famers Tim Hardaway, Mitch Richmond and Chris Mullin. Nelson said he wanted them on the court at the same time.
Nelson spent 11 seasons over two stints with Golden State. The first one was punctuated by a rift with rookie star Chris Webber, who was traded away a month into his second season. Nelson, demoralized by the trade, missed nine games that season due to illness and resigned under pressure three months later in February 1995.
In between, Nelson was fired after less than one season in New York in 1995-96, then coached in Dallas for eight seasons, missing 21 games with the Mavericks starting in December 2000 to recuperate from prostate cancer surgery.
Nelson’s son, Donnie,joined his father as an assistant coach with the Mavericks in 1998, later became general manager and remained with the organization until 2021. Together they persuaded 20-year-old German starDirk Nowitzkito pass up European basketball and join the Mavericks. Don Nelson also developedSteve Nashinto one of the NBA’s top point guards before Nash went on to win back-to-back MVPs with the Phoenix Suns in 2005 and 2006.
“Don Nelson was a true innovator whose influence on the game of basketball is still felt today,” current Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. “He consistently challenged conventional thinking, experimented with different lineups and styles of play and saw possibilities in the game that others often did not. So much of what is now commonplace in the modern NBA can be traced back to the way Nellie approached the game.”
At Golden State, Nelson’s “We Believe” Warriors led by Baron Davis upset Nowitzki and the top-seeded Mavericks in the first round of the 2007 playoffs in one of the biggest shockers in NBA history. In his final season as a coach, Nelson mentored rookie Stephen Curry in 2009-10.
“One of the big reasons I was drafted by the Warriors was because of Don Nelson. The story is he never liked rookies, but from Day 1 he challenged me and gave me an opportunity to be my best self on the court,” Curry said in a statement released by the Warriors. “He taught me a lot during our one season together and I’ll never forget the night he became the winningest coach in NBA history in Minnesota. We were so happy for him. He had an immeasurable impact on the sport and will go down as one of the greatest minds in the history of the game.”
Davis added: “When I think of Nellie, I’ll always think of the ‘We Believe’ team and our incredible run in 2007. He understood what made us go and made us believe we could beat anybody, ultimately helping us make history as the first No. 8 seed to defeat a No. 1 seed in a seven-game series. That time in my life and career was truly special, and Nellie was a huge part of making it possible.”
Nelson retired as the NBA’s career coaching wins leader with 1,335, just ahead of Lenny Wilkens’ 1,332. Nelson kept that top spot for nearly 12 years before close friend and now-retired San Antonio coachGregg Popovich passed him in March 2022.
Nelson was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2012. In 2025, hereceived the Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award, presented by the National Basketball Coaches Association. Miffed that the Mavericks sent Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers in a blockbuster trade, Nelson wore a pair of Doncic’s signature Jordan Brand sneakers to the awards ceremony. He called the tradea “tremendous mistake.”
Born in Muskegon, Michigan, Nelson attended high school in Rock Island, Illinois, and averaged a double-double in college at Iowa. He spent his retirement years living on the Hawaiian island of Maui and owned several short-term rentals on the island.

item.title: 《蜘蛛侠：全新一天》保持创纪录节奏，《奥德赛》创诺兰新高
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——据周日电影公司估计，《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》继续在影院上映，第二个周末的国内​​票房就达到了 1.445 亿美元，而克里斯托弗·诺兰的《奥德赛》则创下了导演的新高。
索尼与漫威联合推出的这部影片在上映短短 10 天内就在全球收获了 16.7 亿美元的票房，有望成为有史以来最卖座的大片之一。在国内，没有哪一部电影能比这更快地获得更高的总票房。迄今为止，《全新一天》在美国和加拿大影院的票房收入已达 6.551 亿美元。在海外，这一数字已经超过10亿美元。
仅用了 7 天，《全新一天》就成为年度票房最高的电影，轻松取代《玩具总动员 5》（全球 10.7 亿美元）。在此之前，索尼电影还没有在第二个周末票房突破 1 亿美元。它差点就打破了 2015 年大二电影票房最高记录：《原力觉醒》，票房为 1.492 亿美元。
克里斯托弗·诺兰的《奥德赛》票房也突破了10亿美元。在上映的第四个周末，环球影业的国内票房收入增加了 3,150 万美元，全球总票房达到 11 亿美元。
诺兰的荷马史诗是自 2012 年《黑暗骑士崛起》以来导演第一部达到这一门槛的电影。现在，在不考虑通货膨胀的情况下，它成为诺兰有史以来票房最高的影片，超过了《黑暗骑士崛起》（10.8 亿美元）和 2009 年的《黑暗骑士》（10 亿美元）。诺兰的《奥本海默》（9.75 亿美元）以略低于里程碑的成绩结束。
当然，这一成功很大一部分归功于 IMAX。《奥德赛》在该公司的大屏幕上获得了 1.473 亿美元的国内票房，现已成为 IMAX 有史以来票房最高的国内影片。
《奥德赛》还剩下一个主要市场。该片将于周五在中国上映。
《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》和《奥德赛》帮助好莱坞创下了自疫情以来的最佳票房年度。根据 Rentrak 的数据，门票销售量比去年增长了 18.5%。已经有五部票房达到 10 亿美元的电影——比 2019 年以来的任何一年都要多。另外两部是《迈克尔》和《超级马里奥银河电影》。
Rentrak 预测周一夏季影院的整体收入将达到 40 亿美元。长期以来，这种季节性标记一直是好莱坞业务蓬勃发展的标志。自疫情爆发以来，唯一一个票房收入超过 40 亿美元的夏季是 2023 年，当时《芭比娃娃》和《奥本海默》带动了票房收入。
根据 Rentrak 的数据，截至周日，夏季收入仅比 40 亿美元少 1,480 万美元。
两部喜剧试图为大片提供一些反制方案，但收效甚微。
威尔·格鲁克 (Will Gluck) 执导的浪漫喜剧《仅限一夜》(One Night Only) 规定婚前性行为为非法，每年只有一晚除外，首映票房为 570 万美元。环球影业发行的影片由莫妮卡·巴巴罗和卡勒姆·特纳主演，制作成本约为 2500 万美元。评论不好（烂番茄上有 46% 的新鲜度），但观众评分（CinemaScore 为“B+”）较好。
排在第四位的是福克斯探照灯公司的《超级士兵 3》，这是喜剧剧团 Broken Lizard 的长篇喜剧系列中的第三部。它首映票房为400万美元。
两部新的限量上映电影挤满了影院。A24 的《托尼》由多米尼克·塞萨 (Dominic Sessa) 饰演年轻的安东尼·波登 (Anthony Bourdain)，票房收入为 348,955 美元，成为年度最佳银幕平均首映票房之一：每家影院 58,159 美元。Mubi 的《瘴气营的青少年性与死亡》由《我看到了电视的光芒》的电影制片人简·舍恩布伦 (Jane Schoenbrun) 执导，首映后在五个银幕上的平均票房为 50,300 美元。
根据 Rentrak 的数据，随着周一公布的最终国内数据，该清单考虑了美国和加拿大影院周五至周日的预计门票销售情况：
1.《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》，1.45亿美元。

item.title: 服装品牌试图用针线赢得 Z 世代的青睐
item.description:
NEW YORK (AP) — Encouraging customers to mend worn clothesinstead ofbuying new ones might seem like a self-defeating sales strategy. But in-store repairs and sewing workshops are becoming essential retail services for clothing brands as they try to appeal to young consumers who want to save money and the planet.
While luxury fashion houses and select specialty retailers like Patagonia and L.L. Bean have offered product repairs for decades, the concept has caught on.Jeans giantLevi Strauss & Co., casual wear chain Uniqlo and budget retailer Primark are a few of the apparel companies hoping to win over Generation Z shoppers with a needle and thread.
Levi’s created a handstitching course for high school students after determining that many members of Gen Z lacked thesewing skillsto match their interest in thrift store shopping and sustainability. Employees spend 90 minutes instructing teenagers on four tasks: sewing on a button, hemming, patching a hole and fixing a tear.
The Wear Longer program, which the San Francisco-based company is expanding across the U.S., builds on the repair and customization services Levi’s offers at hundreds of stores worldwide.
“We think it’s important to empower the people who buy our clothes with the skill sets to maintain them, to get them to that second life,” Paul Dillinger, Levi’s head of global design innovation, said.
Detroit resident Chloe Halprin, 25, is the kind of consumer retailers hope to attract with a“fix it, don’t ditch it”message.
In high school, Halprin shopped at inexpensive, trendy stores. Fixing a big rip felt beyond her limited sewing ability. If she damaged a top or skirt fromForever 21, “I might just throw it away.”
These days, Halprin buys most of her clothes secondhand. She recently learned to hem with a sewing machine and hopes to tackle projects like turning a skirt into a shirt.
“I try to be conscientious of my carbon footprint,” Halprin, a nonprofit grant writer, said. “I really don’t like waste. I’m trying to save money as well.”
The evolution of mending from an economic necessity and traditional craft to a method for cultivating customers didn’t happen overnight. The fashion industry as a whole has come under intensifying pressure to reduce its contributions to environmental pollution andclimate change.
Textile waste— which includes manufacturing remnants, unwanted clothes and linens, and unsold products — is one of the industry’s most pressing challenges. Each year, the world generates fabric waste at a rate equivalent to a garbage truck’s worthgetting dumpedor incinerated every second, the United Nations Environment Program estimates.
Researchers broadly agree that repairing and reselling clothes can reduce a garment’s environmental impact, especially if it delays or replaces a new purchase. But many caution the practices remain too limited to offset continued growth in clothing production and consumption.
Clothing production roughly doubled between 2000 and 2015, while the average number of wearings per garment declined by about 36%, according to figures compiled by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation. The sustainability nonprofit estimated that less than 1% of discarded clothing material got recycled into new apparel.
Enter Generation Z, the cohort born between 1997 and 2012. It’s the generation that grew up with fast fashion and e-commerce, then had school years and young adulthoods shaped bythe coronavirus pandemicandpost-pandemicinflation.
Whether due to limited budgets or a rejection of materialism, Gen Z has helped thepreowned clothing marketgrow much faster than retail apparel sales in the U.S., independent market intelligence firm GlobalData estimated in a report with resale platform ThredUp.
For companies that make new clothes, mending programs and classes address “some deeper consumer needs and consumer behaviors at the moment,” GlobalData retail analyst Neil Saunders said.
The hands-on response from mass-market retailers, especially fast-fashion chains like Primark, Zara and H&M, has generated interest as well as skepticism.
Zara, which has its headquarters in Spain, launched a digital platform in 2022 for customers to resell their used pieces and to request basic alterations and repairs. The program is available in 17 of the nearly 100 countries where the trend-driven retailer operates.
Ireland-based Primark has focused more on customer education. The value-focused retailer hosts free “Love It For Longer” events where customers are taught skills like replacing zippers and buttons.
“Learning how to repair and care for clothing is probably one of the most simplest but absolutely totally effective ways that we can reduce waste and also extend the lifetime of whatever we buy,” Vicki Swain, Primark’s product longevity & partnership lead, said.
The company has held the workshops — more than 730 altogether — in nine of the 17 countries where Primark has stores, including the U.S. Primark also tested in-store repairs at three U.K. locations this year.
Swain argues that affordable clothes can be just as durable and repair-worthy as more expensive ones. Half the items Primark sells annually are basics like socks, underwear, T-shirts, and jeans, she said.
“There is nothing throw away about our products,” Swain said.
Uniqlo, which focuses on timeless wardrobe staples, offers a range of aftercare services, including repairs, decorative sashiko mending, embroidery and creative restyling.
Available in 75 of the Japanese mass-market retailer’s roughly 2,500 stores worldwide, the services are promoted as a national extension of the product life cycle. Providing them also strengthens Uniqlo’s connection with customers, said Jean-Emmanuel Shein, director of global corporate responsibility at Uniqlo USA.
Kate Fletcher, a professor of sustainability, design and fashion systems at Manchester Metropolitan University in England, said she thinks the repair initiatives of popular retailers are well-meaning, but she doubts they will have much environmental impact.
“The fashion sector’s primary source of impact is due to the overproduction of pieces and growing volumes of garments created,” Fletcher said. “Repairing a garment in store happens in addition to these growing production volumes, not instead of them.”
The question facing the fashion industry is whether repairs can evolve from niche service to commercially viable.
Sweden’s H&M Group, which has more than 4,000 stores in over 80 countries, has been unusually candid about one of the biggest obstacles: the economics. The company has argued that repair andresaleare desirable goals, but manufacturing new garments costs businesses less than keeping existing ones in use.
H&M experimented with mending and redesign studios in several European flagship stores over the past decade. The company also is majority owner of a secondhand clothing platform called Sellpy.
In May, H&M joined Primark, ThredUp and dozens of other fashion and textile businesses in signing a statement that urged governments in North America and the European Union to adopt tax policies that would make repairing and reselling clothes profitable.
Making mending work in retail is challenging because it’s labor intensive and must be priced low enough to entice customers, Saunders, of GlobalData, said. Signals from consumers also are mixed, he said.
“I think younger shoppers still shop fast fashion because even though it goes against some of their principles, it is one of the most accessible parts of the market,” Saunders said. “But what they’re doing as well, though, is they’re buying into alternative channels like resale. And they’re having things repaired.”

item.title: 华尔街上涨后，世界股市涨跌互现，而油价则反弹走高
item.description:
曼谷（美联社）——周一，欧洲和亚洲股市涨跌互现，华尔街股市上涨后，日本日经 225 指数领涨。
由于结束中东冲突的努力状况仍不明朗，油价上涨。
欧洲早盘，德国 DAX 指数上涨 0.3%，至 26,411.01 点；巴黎 CAC 40 指数小幅下跌 0.1%，至 8,703.73 点。英国富时 100 指数下跌 0.3%，至 10,869.35 点。
标准普尔 500 指数未来上涨 0.1%，而道琼斯工业平均指数则下跌 0.1%。
在东京，基准日经 225 指数上涨 2.1%，至 66,970.22 点，受到科技公司强劲上涨的推动。
计算机芯片设备制造商Tokyo Electron上涨4.1%，芯片测试设备制造商Advantest上涨6.4%。
在韩国，由于主要芯片制造商的股价下跌，韩国综合指数上涨 0.7%，至 6,299.66 点。三星电子下跌 0.4%，而其规模较小的竞争对手、内存芯片制造商 SK 海力士则下跌 0.1%。
分析师表示，外国投资者正在出售大型科技公司的股票，以锁定近期收益的利润，并将持股重新平衡到国防承包商等其他行业。
香港恒生指数上涨 1.1%，至 25,937.49 点；上证综指上涨 0.7%，至 3,966.59 点。
在澳大利亚，S&P/ASX 200 指数下跌 0.3%，至 9,232.60 点。
台湾的 Taiex 指数飙升 1.6%，印度的 Sensex 指数几乎没有变化。
以色列拒绝美国宣布的协议后油价上涨加沙总统唐纳德·特朗普。伊朗和阿曼之间关于管理霍尔木扎斯德黑兰海峡的潜在协议的细节显示，与“敌对国家”有联系的船只将被禁止。
与此同时，也门伊朗支持的胡塞叛军袭击了该国红海沿岸政府控制的港口，加深了人们对战略航道受到威胁以及可能重新陷入内战的担忧。
国际标准布伦特原油上涨 0.8%，至每桶 84.23 美元。美国基准原油上涨 0.7%，至每桶 78.72 美元。
荷兰合作银行高级宏观策略师巴斯·范格芬（Bas van Geffen）在评论中表示：“谈判代表表示，建立安全航线的协议已经接近达成，但伊朗现在可能正在探索可以从美国获得多少回报。”
本周，投资者将获得美国几项重要的通胀数据，其中最受关注的是消费者价格指数（CPI），该指数衡量消费者的成本。预计 7 月份通胀率为 3.4%，略低于 6 月份的 3.5%。今年大部分时间通胀率一直维持在 3% 以上。
周五，在政府报告雇主上个月意外裁员 23,000 人后，美国股市上涨，国债收益率下跌。
疲软的就业市场引发了人们对美联储可能会等待更长时间才能加息以对抗通胀的希望。这提振了股价，推动所有主要股指连续第二周上涨并创下多项新纪录。
标准普尔 500 指数上涨 0.6%，至 7,757.64 点，创历史新高。道琼斯工业平均指数上涨 0.3%，至 54,036.93 点，略低于周三创下的纪录。纳斯达克综合指数上涨 1.3%，至 26,690.62 点。
总体而言，就业报告使经济中较光明的领域之一黯淡，加剧了人们在高通胀时期对家庭支出的担忧。其中包括对 6 月和 5 月的数据进行了修订，这几个月的就业人数总计削减了 103,000 个。
就业放缓使美联储平衡就业增长与对抗通胀的努力变得更加复杂。较高的利率可以通过减缓经济增长来帮助抑制通货膨胀，但企业会发现在借贷利率上升的情况下扩张更加困难。
与往常一样，科技股对大盘起到了很大的推动作用。Nvidia 上涨 2.3%，Broadcom 上涨 1.7%。
在周一早些时候的其他交易中，美元兑换日元从 157.71 日元升至 158.72 日元。欧元兑美元汇率从 1.1568 美元跌至 1.15617 美元。

item.title: 如何观赏英仙座流星雨，这是一场令人眼花缭乱的夏季灯光秀
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——英仙座夏季灯光秀又回来了——北半球的观赏条件尤其有希望。
周三晚上到周四早上，流星雨的高峰期恰逢西班牙、冰岛和格陵兰岛的日全食以及六颗行星的巡游——尽管观看火球的最佳时间将在日全食之后。
据 NASA 称，在理想条件下，每小时可以看到多达 50 到 100 颗流星。美国流星协会估计，农村地区每小时可以看到 30 到 50 颗流星。
在任何特定的夜晚，黑暗的天空中都可以看到随机的流星。流星雨往往会带来令人眼花缭乱的天象表演，并且每年都会在可预测的时间发生，当时地球穿过彗星（有时还有小行星）留下的碎片痕迹。这些残余物以极高的速度与地球大气层碰撞，产生被称为流星的光条纹。
天体物理学家尼尔·德格拉斯·泰森周日对美联社表示：“彗星的轨道通常会与地球轨道交叉。因此，当它们接近太阳时，太阳会蒸发掉冰，彗星中冻结的大量污垢和垃圾就会被释放出来，并继续围绕太阳运行。”
2024 年 8 月 12 日星期一，瑞士圣马格雷滕贝格一年一度的英仙座流星雨期间，星星和流星被拍到。（Gian Ehrenzeller/Keystone 来自美联社，文件）
英仙座流星雨是 109P/斯威夫特-塔特尔彗星的碎片，这是一颗冰球，每 133 年绕太阳运行一次，直到 2125 年才会回访。对这场流星雨的观测可以追溯到 2000 多年前。
英仙座流星雨多年来一直受到人们的喜爱，因为它们往往会产生明亮的火球。夏季的气温也使这种淋浴很受欢迎。
德克萨斯州麦克唐纳天文台的天文学家扎克·范德博斯说：“我们不必经历寒冷的冬夜才能看到流星的美景。”
在英仙座流星雨的高峰期间，月亮将处于新月相，使观测条件变得更好。
旧金山大学的天文学家阿帕娜·文卡特桑 (Aparna Venkatesan) 表示：“月亮很美丽，但它却是一位天后。”“新月意味着我们没有月光充斥天空，因此你往往会看到更多的流星。”
要观察流星，请在天黑后到户外，远离云层和城市灯光。文卡特桑计划开车前往内华达山脉。
最佳观赏时间是午夜和黎明之间，此时英仙座位于北方天空的高处。流星似乎是从该星座辐射出来的。
抬起头，给眼睛半个小时的时间来适应黑暗。范德博斯建议选择一块天空进行聚焦，直到一道快速、明亮的条纹经过（即使是在你的余光中），并避免看手机。
“这就是它的神奇之处，”范德博斯说。
美联社记者朱莉·沃克在纽约对这篇报道做出了贡献。美联社健康与科学部得到霍华德休斯医学院科学教育部和罗伯特伍德约翰逊基金会的支持。美联社对所有内容全权负责。

item.title: 水豚在冲撞巴西立法机构时保持冷静
item.description:
巴西库亚巴（美联社）——巴西州议会越来越多地发现其投票会场被一群意想不到的访客入侵：水豚。
这些臭名昭著的寒冷啮齿动物漫步穿过巴西中部马托格罗索州库亚巴当地立法大楼的前门，令上周准备投票的立法者感到惊讶。该建筑毗邻一个充满野生动物的公园。
7月30日，工作人员纳亚拉·布埃诺（Nayara Bueno）拍摄了这种原产于南美洲的啮齿动物的意外来访，并试图带领这些哺乳动物转身返回公园。
“他们经常出现在这里，所以我们已经习惯看到他们了，”布埃诺说。
水豚因其异常冷静的举止和高度社交的天性而在全球网络上人气飙升。作为半水生动物，它们在河流、湖泊和湿地附近繁衍生息，通常群居，体重可达 80 公斤（175 磅）。
他们的访问没有对马托格罗索州立法机构造成任何损害。
